questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to do only one—either brake or swerve.
Do not swerve. Use only the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do one action after the other. Do not brake while swerving. Braking and swerving at the same time can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: Which of these should a good face shield NOT have?
questions.explanation: A good face shield should let air pass through. An airtight seal will cause fogging and make it hard to see.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to lower your crash risk?

options.text: Make yourself visible to other drivers.
Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: Do not rely on hope. Instead, be visible, signal your plans, position your bike well, and watch for hazards ahead.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to get off the road faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: Ease off the throttle and stay straight. If you need to brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: True or False: When braking, use only the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which should you NOT do when riding at night?

options.text: Use the headlights of other vehicles to help you see.
Make yourself visible to other drivers.
Ride only on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Change your lane position as needed to see better, be seen, and keep a safe distance from other traffic. Use your high beam (unless following another car), use other vehicles' lights to see, and wear reflective clothing.

questions.question: When you slow down or stop, you should:
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears using the clutch. End in first gear so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Where are motorcycles most likely to have a conflict with other traffic?
questions.explanation: Intersections are the most dangerous place for motorcycle crashes. Watch carefully for other vehicles that may cross in front of you.

questions.question: True or False: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles, often within the first few minutes of riding.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while braking on dry pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and shift down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: Keep the rear brake locked. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested like most food and drinks. What does this mean?

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested, so it enters the bloodstream quickly and reaches the brain within minutes. The body eliminates about one drink per hour.

questions.question: When carrying a motorcycle passenger, you should tell them to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Always give your passenger safety instructions before riding. Have them get on after you start the engine. They should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt. Their feet must stay on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after having one drink before you ride:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and driving.
The alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
The alcohol may still affect you.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The alcohol may still affect you.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even if you drink one drink per hour. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Small vehicles can look ______ away and seem to move ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles may appear farther away and seem to move more slowly than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their true location and speed.

questions.question: Motorcycle passengers must wear a helmet.
questions.explanation: Helmets reduce the risk of head injuries in crashes, but Illinois law does not require passengers to wear them.
